RagShortTexts: Ottokar II joined the Sambian expedition of 1255.
The campaign is associated with Königsberg’s foundation.

Variants.Content: Ottokar II participated in the Sambian expedition of 1255, linking prestige and religious aims with Königsberg’s foundation. Visiting forces had return plans; continued holding depended on those remaining, food and renewed agreements.
A campaign like that of 1255 consumes horses on arrival and return. Remaining guards still patrol and receive supplies after visitors leave; celebration does not replace the next watch.
Prestigious assistance improves leverage but needs duration and provisioning agreed. Counting visitors as permanent troops creates gaps at the new post.
Expeditions bring demand and requisitions. Harvests do not recover on departure; payment and returned tools prevent one season’s hosting from damaging later livelihood.
